test_title: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-II Official Paper-I (Held On: 20 Jan, 2025)
subject: general
question: ABCD is a quadrilateral in which diagonal BD = 70 cm. AL ⊥ BD and CM ⊥ BD such that AL = 18 cm and CM = 20. Find the area (in cm²) of the quadrilateral ABCD.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The area of a general quadrilateral equals half the product of its diagonal and the sum of perpendiculars dropped on it.

⇒ Area = 1/2 × Diagonal × (Sum of perpendiculars)

⇒ Area = 1/2 × 70 × (18 + 20)

⇒ Area = 35 × 38 = 1330

**∴ The correct answer is 1330 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6b5eeaaac182d3d9589fa21812af4e564ccc81e447bcbe47d239cd55e873b364.png] 

**Given:**

Diagonal BD = 70 cm

Perpendicular AL = 18 cm

Perpendicular CM = 20 cm

**Formula Used:**

Area of a triangle = 1/2 × base × height

Area of Quadrilateral ABCD = Area of ΔABD + Area of ΔBCD

**Calculation:**

⇒ Area of ΔABD = 1/2 × BD × AL

⇒ Area of ΔABD = 1/2 × 70 × 18 = 630 cm²

⇒ Area of ΔBCD = 1/2 × BD × CM

⇒ Area of ΔBCD = 1/2 × 70 × 20 = 700 cm²

⇒ Total Area = 630 + 700 = 1330 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 1330 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of Rhombus

The area is calculated as half the product of its diagonals: Area = 1/2 × d₁ × d₂.

Area of Trapezium

Calculated as half the sum of parallel sides multiplied by the distance between them: Area = 1/2 × (a + b) × h.

Cyclic Quadrilateral

A quadrilateral whose vertices all lie on a single circle. Its area can be found using Brahmagupta's formula: Area = √((s−a)(s−b)(s−c)(s−d)), where s is the semi-perimeter.
